analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and an apocopated verb form.

evidence.note: Serug lived two hundred years after he fathered Nahor.

article.name: נָחוֹר
article.summary: In Genesis 11:23, Nahor is the son of Serug. The meaning of the name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נָחוֹר and leave its root unassigned.
draft.definition: Nahor, the personal name borne here by Serug’s son.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:23 names Nahor as the child whom Serug fathered.

analysis.evidence: Genesis 11:23 identifies Nahor as Serug’s son. In 11:24, נָחוֹר follows וַיְחִי as its subject and remains the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד אֶת תָּרַח. Nahor lived twenty-nine years and fathered Terah.
analysis.morphology: Unprefixed Hebrew personal name serving as the subject of the masculine singular verb וַיְחִי.

analysis.evidence: In תֵּשַׁע וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה, “nine and twenty years,” תֵּשַׁע supplies the nine units in Nahor’s age of twenty-nine when he fathered Terah.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Nine as the units component of twenty-nine.
